task: Build Coloring v1, the second minigame of the esl-likes 3D ESL game, as a complete vertical slice: 3D Art Room NPC interaction -> speech -> full-screen 2D brush colouring -> scoring -> back to the 3D room -> give the picture to the NPC -> turnaround. The shared shell, speech stack and the Restaurant already exist and work; this order adds one minigame against the frozen interface.
requirements: Read SPEC.md first: the anti-shortcut rule near the top, section 3 (speech, 'Listening again'), and section 5 (Coloring v1). SPEC.md is the frozen design and wins over any assumption. Also read DESIGN_DECISIONS.md for existing rationale. Do not modify SPEC.md.

Create src/minigames/coloring/ with at least: index.js (createColoring(ctx) controller), scoring.js (PURE logic, no DOM, no three.js), and scoring.test.mjs (node:test). Picture/region data and the 2D painting UI may be further modules in that folder.

createColoring(ctx) implements the frozen interface { id, enter(level), update(dt), exit() }, exactly as src/minigames/placeholder/index.js and src/minigames/restaurant/index.js do. ctx provides { scene, camera, cameraRig, input, speech, audio, dialogue, characters, hud, settings, transitions, finish }. Level is ignored in v1.

Register it: src/main.js minigames map gets ['coloring', createColoring]; in src/config/lesson.js set the coloring lesson available: true and add a UI.coloring block with ALL new Japanese strings. No UI text hardcoded elsewhere.

3D Art Room: compact room, simple procedural geometry, flat bright materials, an easel or table, and an empty picture frame on a wall. One NPC (a Kenney model key that is not characters.playerModel and not used by the Restaurant: use 'b' or 'q'). Player avatar: characters.create({ model: characters.playerModel }). Same WASD movement feel and follow camera as the Restaurant.

FACING CONVENTION (verified the hard way): Kenney models face +z at rotation.y = 0. Movement heading is atan2(move.x, -move.y) turned the short way round — copy the Restaurant's updateMovement exactly. The NPC must face the player and the camera. Do NOT tint Kenney models to express anything.

Flow: walk to the NPC (generous radius) -> the NPC holds up a black-and-white picture -> ask via promptQuestion(ctx, LESSON, { isActive, onAccepted }) from src/systems/speechPrompt.js -> the NPC answers with answerFor(LESSON, favourite) from src/config/lesson.js, spoken and shown via ctx.dialogue -> after the answer, ctx.transitions.run(...) into the full-screen 2D colouring screen -> paint -> できた -> simple result (stars) -> ctx.transitions.run(...) back to the room -> walk to / face the NPC and press Space to give the picture -> NPC reacts happily (emote-yes plus a Japanese thank-you) and the finished picture appears in the wall frame (CanvasTexture of the painting) -> turnaround via promptAnswer(ctx, LESSON, ...) -> finish({ stars, detail: { category: 'color', answer } }).

Picture: ONE robot line-art picture with exactly three large enclosed regions: body, arms, eyes. Regions must be large enough for a Chromebook trackpad (the eyes region too — make it generous, e.g. a wide visor). Bold black outlines drawn ON TOP of the paint so lines stay crisp.

Palette: exactly three swatches — red, blue, yellow — large and clearly different. NO swatch is selected by default; the child must choose one before painting (make the palette invite a choice, e.g. gentle pulse).

Round assignment (anti-shortcut, SPEC 5): each round pick the NPC's favourite colour uniformly from the three AND, independently, the STARRED region uniformly from body/arms/eyes. Implement as a pure pickRound(rng = Math.random) in scoring.js returning { favourite, starred }.

The starred region must be painted in the favourite colour and carries most of the score. The other two regions are FREE (any colour; coverage and neatness only). Do NOT give the free regions target colours — that would reveal the starred colour by elimination.

Nothing may hint at the answer: the star marker on the starred region uses no palette colour (black/white outline star or similar); the NPC and room carry no colour cue tied to the round; no swatch is preselected.

Brush painting, not a fill tool: pointer down + drag paints with a large, forgiving round brush. Interpolate between pointer samples so fast trackpad or mouse movement leaves no gaps. Use pointer capture and touch-action: none. Mouse, touch and Chromebook trackpad click-drag must all work. Painting over an area with another colour replaces it.

Scoring is computed on a coarse grid in scoring.js, not on pixels: build a region map (grid of 0 = background, or a region id) from the picture geometry and a paint grid (0 = unpainted, else palette index + 1) updated from the same stroke geometry as the visible paint. Export a pure scorePainting({ regionMap, paintGrid, width, height, starred, favourite, replayed }) returning { starCorrect, freeCoverage, neatness, ratio, stars }.

Scoring terms: starCorrect = share of starred-region cells painted in the favourite colour; freeCoverage = share of free-region cells painted any colour; neatness = 1 - (painted background cells OUTSIDE a forgiving margin of about 2 cells around the regions) / max(1, painted cells), so small overshoots cost nothing; memory bonus when the answer was never replayed. Suggested ratio = 0.55*starCorrect + 0.2*freeCoverage + 0.15*neatness + 0.1*(replayed ? 0 : 1); stars: >= 0.8 -> 3, >= 0.4 -> 2, else 1; and starCorrect < 0.5 can never give 3 stars.

scoring.test.mjs must cover at least: a perfect picture in the favourite colour scores 3 stars; the same picture with the starred region in a wrong colour scores fewer than 3; scribbling all three colours evenly over the starred region scores fewer than 3; replaying the answer with an otherwise perfect picture still scores 3 (only the bonus is lost); overshoot inside the margin does not lower neatness while paint far outside does; pickRound over several hundred seeded draws produces all 9 favourite x starred combinations; an empty painting scores 1 star.

Listening again (SPEC 3): on the colouring screen offer the shared createListenAgain({ root, label: UI.listenAgain, onPress }) from src/ui/listenAgain.js. Pressing it replays the NPC's answer sentence (audio, plus the sentence shown briefly) and sets replayed = true. It never deducts score; it only forfeits the memory bonus.
The できた button becomes available once a reasonable share of the picture is painted (e.g. 20% of region cells); no timer anywhere.

While the 2D screen is up: hide the 3D HUD and dialogue, and ignore WASD movement in the room. When returning, restore movement and camera. The 3D -> 2D -> 3D transitions must never show a half-built frame.

exit() must dispose every owned geometry, material, texture and canvas, remove overlays, event listeners and injected style elements it owns, and clear speech/hud targets, exactly as the Restaurant does. Entering Coloring twice in a row from the hub must not leak or duplicate anything.
npm test and npm run build must both pass.
constraints: Do NOT modify SPEC.md, src/systems/* , src/ui/*, src/scenes/hub.js, src/styles.css, the Restaurant or the placeholder. If a shared system genuinely lacks something, say so in the summary instead of editing it. The only shared edits allowed: the registry line and import in src/main.js, and in src/config/lesson.js the coloring `available` flag plus a new UI.coloring block.
Do NOT add dependencies. three and vite only.
Do NOT build Drink Stand, Sports or Zoo, a picture library, difficulty levels, a fill tool, an eraser, undo or a timer.
Do NOT build a universal minigame base class or share scoring maths with the Restaurant.
No mouse-look, pointer lock, manual camera rotation or precision movement in the 3D room.

Source-edit hygiene: edit files with structured file tools. If a shell-based edit fails on quoting or escaping, stop editing through the shell for that change and use the file tools; never escalate through nested shell/python/regex patches.
Do not inline code into shell commands; run the declared npm scripts.
notes: Governing rule (SPEC): the NPC's English answer must be information the child needs. For Coloring that means a child who ignores 'I like blue.' can still finish and get a stamp, but can never RELIABLY get the maximum score: the favourite colour and the starred region are both random and independent each round, and nothing on screen hints at either. Please state in your summary how you checked each anti-shortcut leak listed in SPEC (fixed mapping, order, elimination, colour cues, default selection, free trial-and-error). The project already learned several traps: Kenney models face +z; one avatar key (characters.playerModel); tinting textured Kenney models turns skin grey; the dialogue bubble uses width max-content; focused buttons must not swallow movement keys (handled in input.js). Keep the tone calm and creative — this is the calm stage between the busy Restaurant and the fast Drink Stand. Append meaningful design decisions to DESIGN_DECISIONS.md as dated entries. List every file you touched in your summary.
